item.title: Isaias strengthens into Category 2 hurricane on collision course with the Gulf Coast
item.description: The first hurricane of the Atlantic season was forecast to intensify rapidly and cause dangerous conditions in the Florida Panhandle, southern Alabama and southern Mississippi when it makes landfall late Friday or early Saturday.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Study finds 194-year-old tortoise is 'aging more slowly than you would expect'
item.description: Researchers are studying the genome of the world's oldest land animal — a 194-year-old tortoise named Jonathan — to uncover secrets about his longevity.
item.content:encoded: Researchers are studying the genome of the world's oldest land animal — a 194-year-old tortoise named Jonathan — to uncover secrets about his longevity.

item.title: 4 people on NASA's Crew-12 mission return to Earth after 8 months in space
item.description: Four people — two NASA astronauts, one from the European Space Agency and a Russian cosmonaut — spent nearly eight months at the space station, conducting spacewalks, science experiments and research.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Medical debt is crushing hospital patients in LA. Health officials may have a fix
item.description: In Los Angeles County, the nation's most populous, a new system could screen hospital patients for financial aid, preventing hundreds of thousands from getting bills they can't pay.

item.title: This surprising mammal fossil is giving scientists something to chew on
item.description: It's likely you've already chewed and swallowed some tasty morsel today. But when did that ability emerge? New evidence points to at least the middle Jurassic, back when dinosaurs still reigned.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Gut microbes followed migrating humans across continents, new study suggests
item.description: New research looks at the surprising similarities in the gut microbiomes of hunter-gathers in Tanzania and horticulturalists in Bolivia, and asks: What role do these bacteria play in human health?

item.title: Scientists win chemistry Nobel for discoveries about mirrored molecules that led to many drugs
item.description: Scientists Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in chemistry for untangling mysterious mirror images in molecules, a discovery that has been used to develop countless drugs.

item.description: The Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded Francis Halzen of the University of Wisconsin Madison, who built an observatory under Antarctica.
